critical_errors.issue: The citation matches [BMPS26, Proposition 6.13](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08664v1), but its claimed conclusion is incompatible with the explicitly adopted integral-slope convention. Take X=R with primitive rays ±1, weights 1, and gamma(x)=|x|. Define the bounded integral-piecewise-affine obstacle u(x)=0 for x≤1, u(x)=1−x for 1≤x≤2, and u(x)=−1 for x≥2. Its envelope is f(x)=−x for x≤0, f(x)=x/2 for 0≤x≤2, and f(x)=x−1 for x≥2. Indeed, f is convex, lies below gamma+u, and differs boundedly from gamma; every competitor is bounded above by the chord joining (0,0) and (2,1), and elsewhere by the obstacle, which equals f. Thus P_gamma(u)=f has slope 1/2 on (0,2), so it is not piecewise affine in the stipulated integral sense on any subdivision. Textual agreement with the reference does not resolve this explicit contradiction.

repair_hints: [pi_ece35c5be245f9d7cbcc52ef] Distinguish integral-piecewise-affine obstacles from envelopes with possibly nonintegral slopes. Establish the weaker finite affine regularity actually needed and justify the Monge–Ampère/Laplacian identification for those envelopes, or consistently enlarge the function spaces and verify the corrected regularity input. The subsequent perturbation, counterexample, and bounded-shift arguments can then be retained.
